newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Transport strike strands commuters in Karachi.
newsitem.headline: Transport strike strands commuters in Karachi.

text.p: A transport strike on Saturday partially paralysed the southern city of Karachi, Pakistan's commercial hub and main port, witnesses said.
They said many people were stranded at bus stops waiting for the few buses and taxis not observing the strike, which was called by private operators to back demands for higher fares.
Most major shopping centres were at least partly closed and money changers kept their shops shut for fear of violence.
Bankers and dealers at the Karachi Cotton Exchange said business was thin. The Karachi Stock Exchange was closed for its usual Friday-Saturday weekend.

The Karachi Transport Federation said in a statement that the strike had been called to press the government to allow buses, taxis and motorised rickshaws to raise fares to offset a series of fuel price rises in the past few months.

The transport strike coincided with a province-wide strike called by several small religious factions. The factions were protesting the inclusion in the Sindh provincial government of a minister from the Ahmadi religious sect, which they regard as heretical.
Sunni Moslem militants smashed cars and fought police in Karachi on Friday during a demonstration on the same issue.
The militants oppose the appointment of Kanwar Idris as interior and town planning minister in the caretaker provincial cabinet of Chief Minister Mumtaz Bhutto.
Idris belongs to the Ahmadi community, which parliament officially declared to be outside the pale of Islam in 1974.
